segments.zh: 我在星巴克喝杯咖啡，这条线太长了。

segments.en: I was waiting for 20 minutes to get my coffee.
segments.zh: 我等了20分钟才拿到咖啡。

segments.en: Well, Marco, I know that ideas about time and ideas about being late are different in different countries.
segments.zh: 好吧，马可，我知道关于时间和关于迟到的想法的想法在不同的国家是不同的。

segments.en: Yeah, in different countries, people treat time or being on time in different ways.
segments.zh: 是的，在不同的国家，人们以不同的方式对待时间或准时。

segments.en: Yeah, like I'm from Canada and I look at being on time really different than you do, right?
segments.zh: 是的，就像我来自加拿大一样，我认为准时与你真的不同，对吧？

segments.en: Yes, because for example, if you call for a meeting at nine o'clock, usually people will be there at nine o'clock because the meeting will start.
segments.zh: 是的，因为例如，如果您在九点召开会议，通常人们会在九点钟到场，因为会议将开始。

segments.en: In America.
segments.zh: 在美国。

segments.en: Right, in America.
segments.zh: 对，在美国。

segments.en: Now, for example, in Latin America, we do have this, what we call sometimes the Latino time or Hispanic time, which is like nine o'clock is like the time that everyone should be there.
segments.zh: 现在，例如，在拉丁美洲，我们确实有这个，有时我们称之为拉丁裔时间或西班牙裔时间，就像九点钟一样，就像每个人都应该在那里的时间一样。

segments.en: But until people get there, get their coffee and whatever, then it'll be 9.15, maybe up to 9.30.
segments.zh: 但在人们到达那里之前，喝咖啡之类的，然后它会是 9.15，可能高达 9.30。

segments.en: And I think it's a little bit even more noticeable when we're talking about social events.
segments.zh: 而且我认为当我们谈论社交活动时，它会更加明显。

segments.en: Like if you go to someone's house for dinner in Canada, if they say, come to my house at six o'clock for dinner, you'll be there at 6.05, right?
segments.zh: 就像如果你在加拿大某人家吃饭，如果他们说，六点钟来我家吃晚饭，你会在 6.05 到那里，对吧？

segments.en: Okay, yeah.
segments.zh: 好吧，是的。

segments.en: Yeah, usually you'll be there only a couple of minutes after the time that was specified just to, you know, give the house owner a little bit of time.
segments.zh: 是的，通常你会在指定的时间之后到达那里，你知道，给房主一点时间。

segments.en: But if we have a dinner invitation for six, we know that it's not really going to begin eating at six, so people will get there at 6.30 or seven.
segments.zh: 但是，如果我们有六人的晚餐邀请，我们知道它不会真正开始在六点吃饭，所以人们会在 6.30 或 7 点到达那里。

segments.en: And of course, food isn't ready until like maybe eight or nine.
segments.zh: 当然，直到大约八九点，食物才准备好。

segments.en: But in German countries, from what I know, you've got to be there.
segments.zh: 但在德国国家，据我所知，你必须在那里。

segments.en: If they say be there at six, you're there at 6.00, right?
segments.zh: 如果他们说在六点钟到，你在 6 点到，对吧？

segments.en: And also, I think it's about when people start work, right?
segments.zh: 而且，我认为这是人们何时开始工作，对吧？

segments.en: How on time you have to begin work.
segments.zh: 你必须如何准时开始工作。

segments.en: Sometimes it's acceptable to be 10 or 15 minutes so-called late, but in other places, you know.
segments.zh: 有时可以接受所谓的迟到 10 或 15 分钟，但在其他地方，你知道的。

segments.en: Yeah, North America, if you're supposed to start work at nine, you have to be at your desk working at nine.
segments.zh: 是的，北美，如果你应该在九点开始工作，你必须在九点工作。

segments.en: At nine.
segments.zh: 九点。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Yeah, see that in other countries, people get there at nine, get their coffee, maybe take a quick glance at their emails or the newspaper and then, you know, start working at around 9.30 or 10.
segments.zh: 是的，看到在其他国家，人们在九点到达那里，喝咖啡，也许快速浏览一下他们的电子邮件或报纸，然后，你知道，在 9.30 或 10 左右开始工作。

segments.en: So I guess the important thing is to know what the tradition is in the country where you are.
segments.zh: 所以我想重要的是要知道你所在的国家的传统是什么。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So come to our website, EnglishPod.com and let us know how it works in your countries.
segments.zh: 因此，请访问我们的网站 englishpod.com，让我们知道它在您所在国家/地区的运作方式。

segments.en: I know that many different countries have a different way of treating time, so share it with us.
segments.zh: 我知道许多不同的国家处理时间的方式不同，所以与我们分享。

segments.en: Yes, and remember, if you have any questions, please ask them at the website as well.
segments.zh: 是的，请记住，如果您有任何问题，请在网站上提问。

segments.en: We're out of time today, but until next time, thanks for listening and goodbye.
segments.zh: 我们今天没时间了，但直到下一次，感谢您的收听和再见。

segments.en: Bye-bye.
segments.zh: 拜拜。
